Upon disconnection from the ship, a small amount of CO may be 2 2 released from the loading arms, but most of it is captured in the drain header. 4.7.3 TURNDOWN / REDUCED PIPELINE CO SUPPLY 2 The liquefaction plant is designed to function with reduced CO inlet flow rates, allowing operation 2 between approximately 10% to 100% of capacity. At throughputs below 50% of plant rated capacity one liquefaction train is shutdown or put into recycle (depending on anticipated duration) and single train operation continues. Compressor speed control enables a compression train to operate efficiently at flow rates as low as 50% to 70% of its design flow. Below this throughput the compressors will operate in a recycle mode, reducing the plant efficiency. In this mode safety and product quality are not compromised, although the power consumption per ton of CO liquefied will increase compared to 'normal' operations. 2 This mode of operation will support tanker loading operations, although at lower throughputs. Therefore, it will be necessary to reduce the frequency of shipments to ensure sufficient LCO product is in storage 2 ready for shipping. 4.7.4 NO PIPELINE CO SUPPLY 2 This mode of operation would occur if the local CO gathering network is shutdown either through 2 maintenance or failure of a component. In this instance the liquefaction plant would be shut down with compressors, air cooler fans, and transfer pumps shut down. For unscheduled or short duration shutdowns the plant will remain filled with liquid and pressurized while relying on insulation to slow down heat ingress. If the situation persists, heat ingress will cause the CO to vaporize. The resulting pressure increase will cause the PCVs to open under the 2 control of the plant’s Integrated Control and Safety System (ICSS), allowing CO gas to vent to the vent 2 stack. Provided power is still available from the external power grid, the instrument air system will continue to operate, providing control / actuating air to valves through the process. This will allow the plant operators an opportunity to manage the boil off through the control system. Eventually, the plant will be liquid-free and still under pressure. During this time it will be possible to receive cargos of Liquid CO via truck or rail car and load marine 2 tankers. However, it would not be possible to recover any displaced CO gas and this would be routed to 2 the vent stack and lost to the environment. 4.7.5 LOSS OF POWER This is an upset mode of operation, and would be one of the cases considered when defining the control and safety system and mechanical relief devices. Loss of power would immediately shut down all electric motors on the site including compressors, air coolers, and transfer / loading pumps. All operations would cease until power was restored.
